articles.originalTitle: Russian strikes damage historic buildings in Kyiv and Odesa, including World Heritage sites - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Russian Strikes Damage Historic Buildings in Kyiv and Odesa
articles.excerpt: Multiple cultural heritage sites in Ukraine, including UNESCO-listed locations in Kyiv and Odesa, sustained damage during recent Russian attacks.
articles.content: Russian strikes on November 19 and 20 damaged multiple heritage sites in Ukraine, including the UNESCO-listed St. Michael's Golden-Domed Cathedral and Monastery complex, the frescoed St. Volodymyr's Cathedral in Kyiv, and 12 cultural heritage sites in Odesa. Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Tetyana Berezhna reported that the Volodymyr Cathedral sustained damage to structural elements and paintings. Built in the 19th century, the neo-Byzantine cathedral features art by prominent historical painters. The adjacent Austrian embassy was also damaged in the attack. UNESCO issued a condemnation, noting that historic structures within Odesa's World Heritage property, including the 1834 Kalio Palace, suffered damage. The strikes occurred amid heightened tensions following attacks on the Kerch Bridge, statements by Russian leadership rejecting partial ceasefires, and remarks by US President Donald Trump regarding peace efforts. Meanwhile, several European countries are seeking to bar Russia from participating in the 2027 Architecture Biennale.

articles.originalTitle: angelo renna’s eight principles for welcoming non-human life back into our cities - Designboom
articles.title: Eight Principles for Welcoming Non-Human Life into Urban Design
articles.excerpt: Designer Angelo Renna has published an eight-principle guide for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The recommendations focus on allowing spontaneous green growth, reducing lawn maintenance, and incorporating natural habitats.
articles.content: As human activities over the past half-century have contributed to a significant decline in global wildlife populations, designer Angelo Renna has outlined an eight-principle framework for integrating non-human species into urban environments. The guidelines advocate for allowing urban ecosystems to emerge naturally without excessive landscaping control, alongside reducing the frequency of intensive lawn mowing, which research links to decreased plant and invertebrate diversity. Additional principles include incorporating decaying tree trunks and snags to provide food and shelter for various organisms, providing water sources beyond simple drinking facilities for amphibians and insects, and utilizing porous construction materials and dry-stacked bricks to form microhabitats. The framework also emphasizes choosing diverse multispecies vegetation communities over monocultures to increase ecological resilience against environmental stress. Ultimately, the proposals envision the future city not merely as a human-centric development process, but as a shared habitat characterized by interspecific co-evolution and coexistence between humans and other forms of life.

articles.originalTitle: Conservation of the ‘Sistine Chapel of the Andes’ nears completion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Conservation of the Historic Church Known as the Sistine Chapel of the Andes Nears Completion
articles.excerpt: Conservation work focusing on roofs, stone buttresses, and adobe walls at Santiago de Curahuara de Carangas, one of Bolivia's oldest churches, is coming to an end.
articles.content: Conservation projects at the Santiago de Curahuara de Carangas church in the Bolivian Andes, located nearly 4,000 meters above sea level and known as the Sistine Chapel of the Andes due to its impressive murals, are nearing completion. The work, which began in May, was financed by the US Department of State's Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation. Declared a National Monument in 1960, the church was built by Augustinians between the late 16th and early 17th centuries. Project architect Josefina Matas stated that maintaining the roof in good condition is essential to protect the paintings. The restoration team used a unique local technique, placing straw on hollow cane mats to build more resilient roofs. Road protests in May delayed material shipments, pushing completion back by one month. The church houses murals finished in 1777 depicting the Nativity, the Last Supper, and the Last Judgment. Oruro Bishop Krzysztof Białasik submitted the project for US funding. A mass with the bishop and apostolic nuncio is scheduled for December 15 to celebrate the completion of the conservation.

The artist's debut U.S. solo exhibition is on view at the Wexner Center for the Arts in Ohio through February 14, 2027, exploring the connections between European decorative arts and colonial history. Concurrently participating in the Venice Biennale, Baloji is showing three sculptures and 16 collage prints in the main exhibition, alongside contributions to the national pavilion of the Democratic Republic of Congo. Having cofounded the Picha Art and Research Center and the Lubumbashi Biennale in 2008, Baloji aims to support local artists and foster dialogues surrounding ecological crises and extractivism. The artist's research-oriented practice unfolds across various mediums, including video, sculpture, and photography.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: From Constantinople to Istanbul: One City Shared by Two Empires
articles.excerpt: Established as a new imperial capital by Constantine I, the city served as a vital center bridging two distinct cultural traditions across Byzantine and Ottoman eras.
articles.content: In 324 CE, Roman Emperor Constantine I selected the ancient city of Byzantion as his new capital, naming it Nova Roma. Soon known as Constantinople, it became the seat of the Byzantine Empire until 1453. Following the fall of the Byzantine capital, the city rose as Istanbul, serving as the Ottoman capital until 1922. Situated at the crossroads of Europe and Asia along major sea routes, the metropolis flourished through monumental architecture, the Theodosian Land Walls, and the ancient Aqueduct of Valens. Over sixteen centuries, the religious landscape shifted from Roman paganism through Christianity to a majority Islamic identity. Artistic traditions also evolved; while Byzantine Constantinople emphasized sacred images in public spaces, the Ottomans expressed reverence through sophisticated calligraphy. The city accumulated numerous Christian relics, reinforcing its status as a new Jerusalem. Artifacts such as carved gemstone cameos and pectoral crosses reflect both personal devotion and the intersection of classical antiquity with medieval imperial culture. Monumental remnants, including restoration inscriptions and sculptural fragments from the Golden Gate, document the enduring historical layers of a metropolis defined by its strategic importance and diverse heritage.

articles.originalTitle: Connecting Old and New Through a Ceramic Facade - ArchDaily
articles.title: Industrial Complex in Beniel Upgraded with Custom Ceramic Facade
articles.excerpt: Martín Lejarraga Oficina de Arquitectura refurbished the HTBA industrial complex in Beniel. Developed by FAVEKER, a custom ceramic envelope unifies the refurbished structures with a shared architectural identity.
articles.content: At the HTBA facility manufacturing bioactive ingredients for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and food industries, refurbishment and extension works were expressed through a ceramic envelope respecting production logic. Two buildings near the entrance were wrapped in a white ceramic ventilated facade developed specifically by FAVEKER. Three-dimensional extruded ceramic pieces named Brooklyn and Sidney introduce varying depth and movement, interacting with daylight. The project incorporates 998.84 square meters of FAVEKER ceramic facade, divided between 647.64 square meters on the office building and 351.20 square meters on the changing-room pavilion. Installed vertically using the FTS 505 system, the pieces form a continuous sequence emphasizing proportions. A red metal cornice introduces corporate color and contrasts with the ceramic surface. Developed to address specific architectural needs at the site, the ceramic pieces were subsequently added to the manufacturer catalog.

articles.originalTitle: ‘Strain and Resilience’: Alma Allen at Perrotin Paris - ArtReview
articles.title: Alma Allen Presents Monumental Bronze Sculptures at Perrotin in Paris
articles.excerpt: Perrotin Paris is hosting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition featuring a new body of monumental bronze sculptures and wall reliefs exploring touch and memory.
articles.content: Perrotin is presenting Alma Allen's first solo exhibition with the gallery at its Paris space located at 10 impasse Saint-Claude. On view from October 17 through December 19, the exhibition introduces a new body of monumental bronze sculptures that explore touch, transformation, memory, and perception. Each sculpture shares the deliberately unfinished designation Not Yet Titled, reflecting the artist's belief that meaning should remain open. The self-taught sculptor develops small models directly with his hands using string, clay, or wax, a practice that began during his teenage years in Utah. These small models are scanned, enlarged, and cast in bronze at the artist's home foundry. Alongside the freestanding sculptures, the exhibition features bronze wall reliefs whose ridged surfaces bear the appearance of material kneaded by hand. Their visual language connects to Native American petroglyphs, saguaro cactus ribs, and Renaissance drapery. The new works occupy the uncertain space between the physical and the mysterious, inviting viewers to remain open to meanings that reveal themselves over time.

articles.originalTitle: The spirits of Barragán and Legorreta inform a new co-living building in LA - Wallpaper*
articles.title: New Co-Living Building Completed in Los Angeles Echo Park

articles.content: Constructed in the Echo Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, a new co-living building accommodates a total of 26 individual rooms across four storeys. Utilizing a sloping hillside site, the building presents a domestic scale from the street while stepping down to four levels. articles.originalTitle: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190m at Sotheby’s following Nazi loot claims - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Van Gogh painting achieves record 190.4 million dollars at New York auction
articles.excerpt: One of Vincent van Gogh's final paintings sold for 190.4 million dollars with fees at Sotheby's, breaking the artist's auction record following a settlement regarding Nazi-era provenance claims.
articles.content: Vincent van Gogh's 1890 painting Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for 165 million dollars, totaling 190.4 million dollars with fees, at Sotheby's New York, breaking the artist's previous auction record. Long kept out of public view in the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, the artwork went to a room bidder after nearly five minutes of competition. Just a day before the event, Sotheby's announced a settlement between the Blaquier heirs and the heirs of previous owners Hedwig and Samuel Fischer regarding Nazi-era provenance questions. The result makes the painting the second most valuable object ever sold at Sotheby's and the fourth most valuable painting at auction. Back-to-back New York sales generated a combined 777.8 million dollars with fees. Additional auction records were set by Mary Cassatt and Aaron Douglas. Douglas's Harriet Tubman hammered at 12 million dollars, reaching 14.48 million dollars with fees, with proceeds to benefit Bennett College. Cassatt's Summertime fetched 13.3 million dollars with fees, surpassing its estimate. Six lots from the Blaquier-Arrieta collection hammered below low estimates, while the Modern Evening sale achieved 365.8 million dollars with fees amid patchy bidding.

articles.originalTitle: floating concrete cylinder suspends over water basin for buddhist memorial in japan - Designboom
articles.title: Buddhist Memorial Structure Designed for Fukuden-ji Temple in Odawara
articles.excerpt: Located on the grounds of the 1136 Fukuden-ji Temple in Odawara, Japan, the Perpetual Care Grave is a memorial structure designed by architectural practice ASSISTANT. Suspended over a water basin, the concrete cylinder represents the boundary between the living and the departed.
articles.content: Situated on the grounds of the Shingon Buddhist temple Fukuden-ji in Odawara, Japan, the Perpetual Care Grave was designed by architectural practice ASSISTANT. Giving physical form to the boundary between Shigan, the realm of the living, and Higan, the realm of the departed, the monument serves as an architectural threshold for contemplation. The spatial composition relies on elementary geometric forms referencing the Five Elements of Esoteric Buddhism. Suspended over a shallow reflecting basin fed by Odawara's groundwater, the cast-concrete drum appears to hover between the water plane and the sky. Visitors enter along a narrow approach framed by layered rammed-earth walls, passing through an aperture into an open-top interior chamber framing a circular oculus of the sky. Pairing industrial concrete with compacted earth highlights material weathering. Megumi Matsubara and Hiroi Ariyama served as lead architects for the project. Structural engineering was handled by Hirotsugu Tsuboi Structural Engineering Company, and construction was completed by Hamano Construction within a 225-square-meter site area.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul Exhibition Explores Sixteen Centuries of Art at V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum presents Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition featuring over 200 objects that explore 1,600 years of artistic production across the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a comprehensive exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, which runs until 9 May 2027. The exhibition explores 1,600 years of artistic production spanning from AD 330 to 1922. It examines the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond, highlighting the distinct yet connected traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. The display showcases more than 200 objects across four main sections, featuring rare decorative arts, fine silks, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, manuscripts, and paintings. The exhibition is organized into four thematic sections: Roman Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. The opening section covers the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire, followed by sections exploring sacred imagery in Christianity, the visual spectacle of Ottoman court authority, and the cosmopolitan rhythms of urban life characterized by diverse languages and faiths. The exhibition concludes by tracing the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century European culture.

articles.originalTitle: BIG stacks timber volumes with alpine views for new neighborhood in switzerland - Designboom
articles.title: Bjarke Ingels Group Unveils Timber District Proposal for Thun, Switzerland
articles.excerpt: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for Nachwachsende Stadt, a four-building timber district in Thun, Switzerland. The 13000-square-meter development integrates hotel and residential functions within the city's emerging Siegenthalergut neighborhood.
articles.content: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for Nachwachsende Stadt, a four-building timber district designed for the western entrance of Thun's emerging Siegenthalergut neighborhood in Switzerland. Selected through a competition organized by Frutiger AG and the city of Thun, the 13000-square-meter development combines hotel and residential volumes against the backdrop of the Bernese Alps. The southwest corner houses a three-star and a four-star hotel under a shared roof, featuring outdoor terraces and a rooftop restaurant. The eastern buildings accommodate residences with flexible layouts, projecting bays, and balconies facing an internal garden courtyard. Of the total area, approximately 6500 square meters are dedicated to residential uses, 6000 square meters to hotel space, and 400 square meters to commercial activities. All four timber structures are engineered for future disassembly and component reuse to reduce embodied carbon. Environmental systems include green roofs, rainwater retention, and approximately 1800 square meters of photovoltaic panels. The development targets Switzerland's SNBS Gold sustainability certification, with construction on the initial buildings anticipated to begin from 2028.

articles.originalTitle: AOM Higher Education/Research: Utah State University Kem & Carolyn Gardner Learning & Leadership Building - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Utah State University Opens Mass Timber Learning and Leadership Building
articles.excerpt: The Kem and Carolyn Gardner Learning and Leadership Building at Utah State University serves as the institution's first mass timber structure. The facility brings together five academic centers from the Jon M. Huntsman School of Business.
articles.content:
Located on the Utah State University campus, the Kem and Carolyn Gardner Learning and Leadership Building is a 44,658-square-foot, three-story academic facility. The project consolidates five academic centers from the university's Jon M. Huntsman School of Business under one roof. Built by Jacobsen Construction, the facility utilizes a hybrid steel and mass timber system, marking the institution's first mass timber building.

The design features exposed glulam columns and cross-laminated timber decking, creating a light-filled interior inspired by nearby Logan Canyon. This mass timber structure supports the university's goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2040. Through collaboration with Timberlab during design development, structural, mechanical, and electrical systems were concealed within cavities to preserve the visual continuity of the timber.

articles.originalTitle: Happy birthday to the Lloyd's Building! The iconic London tower turns 40 - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Iconic Lloyd's Building in London Celebrates Its Fortieth Anniversary
articles.excerpt: Located in the British capital and designed by Richard Rogers Partnership, the Lloyd's Building is celebrating its 40th anniversary. The 14-storey high-rise places service towers externally, offering a flexible and uninterrupted interior space.
articles.content: Situated in the heart of the British capital, the Lloyd's Building was completed in 1986 to a design by Richard Rogers Partnership. RSHP, the firm's current evolution, is celebrating the 40th anniversary of the landmark High Tech architecture project. Spanning 14 storeys across three towers, the structure places service hubs externally as part of an approach prioritizing material honesty and flexibility. Servant zones such as stairs, lifts, and bathrooms stand freely outside the building mass, allowing for easy access, maintenance, and replacement while leaving a flexible trading floor at the center. These volumes surround a central 60-meter-high, naturally lit atrium. The metallic and glass surfaces reflected the growth and innovation of the era's insurance market. Upon completion, the building received mixed reviews before winning a RIBA award in 1988. Historic England later designated it as one of the key buildings of the modern epoch, making it the youngest building to receive a Grade I listing a mere 25 years after completion.

articles.originalTitle: Construction Starts on $246M Niagara Falls Power Station Hotel Conversion - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Historic Niagara Falls Power Station Converted Into Luxury Hotel
articles.excerpt: Construction has begun on a privately financed redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to convert the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station near Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex, with completion expected in 2029.
articles.content: Construction has commenced on a redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to transform the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station overlooking Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex. Owned by the Ontario provincial agency Niagara Parks, the historic facility is being redeveloped by Toronto Power Hotel Inc., a partnership overseeing the privately financed project. Deltera Contracting Inc. serves as the general contractor, with +VG Architects and MT Planners on the project team. Designed by E.J. Lennox, the steel-frame building opened in 1906 and operated until 1974. The preservation effort will maintain key architectural features while adding a five-star hotel, multiple restaurants, a wellness spa, event facilities, an art gallery, a museum, and public viewing areas. Audited financial statements indicate that approximately 6.72 million dollars in stabilization obligations were transferred to Society Land Holdings Inc. under a long-term lease. Substantial construction completion is anticipated in 2029, with the hotel opening scheduled for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: New Center Housing Retired Space Shuttle Endeavour Unveiled in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center has been completed to house Endeavour, the world's only space shuttle exhibited in launch position. The 450 million dollar project required complex seismic analysis and engineering feats.
articles.content:
The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center inside the California Science Center in Los Angeles was unveiled on November 13. The 200,000-square-foot facility, completed at a cost of 450 million dollars, houses Endeavour, the only space shuttle in the world exhibited in launch position. ZGF Architects, general contractor MATT Construction, and a team of engineers designed a 200-foot-tall curvilinear stainless-steel structure tailored to the geometry of the shuttle stack.

Project director Dennis R. Jenkins noted that seismic analysis was the most challenging aspect. Because civil and aerospace engineers operate under different frameworks, teams had to account for how a seismic event could impact the fragile shuttle stack, valued at 2 billion dollars by NASA. Six triple-friction pendulum isolator bearings separate the supporting concrete pad, allowing the shuttle to glide independently during earthquakes.

During construction, MATT Construction enforced strict safety protocols. Due to the fragile thermal silica tiles, every tool and bolt was tied off with lanyards. BrandSafway engineered specialized free-standing scaffolding that allowed the external fuel tank to be guided inside without touching the orbiter. To avoid dwarfing neighboring facilities, the center was designed 25 feet below grade.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel

articles.content: Situated at the cultural crossroads of the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to unite the international art world from December 4 to 6, 2026. articles.originalTitle: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Birthday Exhibition at the Paris Mint - WWD
articles.title: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Exhibition at the Paris Mint
articles.excerpt: Grasse-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is opening a centenary exhibition featuring more than 250 works and objects at the Paris Mint.
articles.content: Frane-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is celebrating its centenary with a major exhibition at the Paris Mint. Entitled "Fragonard: 100 Years of Collections and Savoir-Faire," the event gathers more than 250 works and objects from the house's heritage collection. The exhibition remains open to the public through Jan. 17, 2027. Company chief executive officer Agnès Costa Webster noted that paintings from the family's collection in Grasse have been brought to Paris for the first time. Hosted at the 18th-century Hôtel de la Monnaie, the multisensory exhibition features paintings, perfume bottles, historic garments, silverware, and personal grooming accessories. articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead and 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Near Construction Site
articles.excerpt: An adjoining 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, New York, leaving 8 people dead and 18 injured. Authorities have launched multiple investigations into the incident.
articles.content: On November 11, a three-story building collapsed into an adjoining excavation site in the Brooklyn borough of New York, resulting in 8 fatalities and 18 injuries. Officials confirmed the dead included two children and two construction workers, while the Fire Department concluded rescue operations on November 12. City records list Townhouse Builders as the general contractor for the project at 2625 Bedford Ave. A project geotechnical report had warned that abutting structures required underpinning and that construction-related vibrations could adversely affect neighboring properties. A March 5 preconstruction survey documented visible cracking at 1321 Flatbush Ave., rating its north masonry facade as poor and its other facades as fair. Area residents reported feeling heavy impacts and shaking while construction was underway next door. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites linked to companies involved in the project. New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, alongside a separate probe launched by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez. The exact cause of the structural collapse remains undetermined pending the conclusion of ongoing investigations by municipal authorities.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Grants Designers Creative Freedom Away From Commerce
articles.excerpt: The new exhibition at the Molteni Museum in Giussano, Italy, offers prominent furniture designers the opportunity to reinterpret existing Molteni Group products without commercial and engineering constraints.
articles.content: Opening at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, a new exhibition provides creative figures in the furniture industry with a platform to produce one-off works free from commercial concerns. The collaborative showcase features creations by Ron Gilad, Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners, Patricia Urquiola, the late Luca Meda, and Vincent Van Duysen. According to Ron Gilad, the initiative aimed to celebrate living creators rather than historical icons. Designers used existing items from the firm as starting points for experimental approaches. Herzog & de Meuron incorporated inflatable cushions into Porta Volta chairs, while OMA reinterpreted tables from the Principles collection in black and powder pink hues. AMDL Circle adapted the MDL System with unconventional contours. Molteni Group announced that the exhibition will remain on display for one year and is expected to travel to additional international cities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | LERATO SHADI | Unfolding - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Lerato Shadi's Performance Unfolding To Be Presented At Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Lerato Shadi's performance titled Unfolding, focusing on memory and collective processes, will meet audiences on November 21, 2026, within Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Shaped around memory, visibility, and collective processes, Unfolding is structured as a performance examining how meaning is produced and transmitted through bodies. The event will take place on November 21, 2026, from 12:00 to 12:40 in the Sala d’Armi E space. The work unfolds through a group relay structure where participants move to the stage, wrap a stone with red wool, and pass the transformed object to another participant. Through this repeated action, the object gradually changes form, accumulating time, touch, and traces of multiple hands. While wrapping becomes a gesture of protection and connection, passing the stone evokes histories and knowledge carried collectively rather than individually. Featuring Camille Badirou, Trovania Dellile, Viviana Medina, Rebecca Pokua Korang, and the artist herself, attendance requires a valid Biennale Arte 2026 admission ticket.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | YO-E RYOU | Breath Orchestra: Score for Silence - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Live Performances and Breath Orchestra at the Venice Biennale Arsenale
articles.excerpt: The Arsenale at the Venice Biennale will host YO-E RYOU Breath Orchestra: Score for Silence, a series of live performances drawing inspiration from the traditions of Haenyeo freedivers.
articles.content: Set within the Arsenale on 21 November 2026 from 14:00 to 14:35, YO-E RYOU Breath Orchestra: Score for Silence presents a series of live orchestrations building upon the artist's audiovisual installation. Performers gather through attentive acts of listening and breathing in a workshop-performance format. Rooted in hydrofeminist research and the traditions of the Haenyeo community of women who freedive to collect food from the sea, the work incorporates moments of breath-holding and silence from underwater labor as an act of transmission and collective learning. The participating performers include Young Sun Kong, who also serves as choreographic advisor, alongside Jiin Gook, Emy Mårtensson Liljegren, Kim Han Yeonji, Hearin Jeong, KkotShin Im, Suhwa Kim, Bitna Youn, and Hayun Kim. The creative team features vocal advisor Jinsol Yu, wearable objects designer Yumi Lee, and creative process facilitator Jiwool Yang. Valid admission for Biennale Arte 2026 is required to attend.

articles.originalTitle: Claude Monet | Waterlilies | L1406 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Claude Monet's 1905 Waterlilies Painting on Display in London
articles.excerpt: Claude Monet's 1905 painting Waterlilies forms part of his series inspired by his water gardens in Giverny. The artwork is housed at the National Gallery in London.
articles.content: After renting a house in Giverny west of Paris in 1883, Claude Monet eventually purchased the property and transformed the grounds into water gardens. Once the gardens matured, Monet turned to depicting them, making the water garden the subject of more than two hundred pictures. Between 1905 and 1908, he painted over sixty views of the pond exploring the contrast between tangible flowers and lily pads and the reflections of the unseen sky and overhanging trees. Housed at the National Gallery in London, Waterlilies exemplifies this series. In the painting, white flowers closest to the viewer feature purple accents for depth, while receding flowers are rendered in simple touches of white, yellow, pink, and red. The water itself consists of myriad tones of violets, blues, turquoise, and greens. The painting was included in Monet's 1909 exhibition at Durand-Ruel's gallery in Paris. Measuring 87 by 100 cm, the oil on canvas work is part of the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.
